jewelry.name: pouch
jewelry.title: pouch
jewelry.reason: A hide pouch with characteristic Cree-style floral beadwork in bright glass beads, matching known Cree/Métis beadwork traditions of the Canadian Subarctic.

jewelry.name: ornament
jewelry.title: ornament
jewelry.reason: A moosehide strip densely decorated with floral glass-bead embroidery, described as Cree work from Island Hake/Manitoba — a classic Subarctic Cree beadwork ornament (likely a garment trim or cuff).

garment.name: Hood
garment.title: Hood
garment.reason: The image shows a beaded and embroidered wool hood with a characteristic floral beadwork pattern, fringe, and quillwork/beadwork style consistent with James Bay Cree craft traditions, matching the claimed ethnicity and category.

garment.name: jacket
garment.title: jacket
garment.reason: A smoked mooseskin pullover jacket with hood, fringing, and buttons, attributed by the museum to Cree makers—a well-known traditional Subarctic Cree garment type.

garment.name: mitten
garment.title: mitten
garment.reason: A pair of smoked mooseskin mittens with silk floral embroidery and beaded/wool-cord tie, a classic Northern Cree craft item worn for cold weather, directly attributed by the museum to Cree makers.

garment.name: boot
garment.title: boot
garment.reason: A soft-soled hide boot with floral cotton embroidery, skin fringe, and wool pompom tie — a classic Cree footwear type, consistent with the claimed maker attribution.

garment.name: Legging strips
garment.title: Legging Panels
garment.reason: Beaded wool legging panels with floral motifs, consistent with Eastern Cree beadwork tradition; matches claimed ethnicity and garment category.

garment.name: pouch
garment.title: pouch
garment.reason: A small felted-wool shot pouch with floral embroidery and a finger-woven wool carrying strap, museum-attributed to Cree makers; this beaded/embroidered floral pouch style is characteristic of Cree and related Subarctic/Woodlands work.

garment.name: cap
garment.title: cap
garment.reason: A handmade baby's cap of cloth with ties, attributed by the museum to Cree makers; this is a plausible garment type for the culture and shows craft made by the claimed people.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard; photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Documentary photo of four Cree men at The Pas, Manitoba, wearing fur/pelt garments and hats, holding large bundles of trapped animal pelts—clearly depicting Cree trapping life and dress.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Studio portrait of a named Cree chief, Kah-mi-yo-ki-suck-way (Fine Day), in horned headdress, fur, breechcloth, belt, and moccasins, holding a flintlock musket — a documentary photograph of Cree dress and regalia, matching the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard (black & white with colour); photographic print
photo.reason: Documentary postcard photo showing two Cree men and a Cree woman with a birchbark canoe and tipi at a lakeside camp — this depicts Cree material culture and daily life as claimed.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Studio profile portrait of a named Cree man wearing traditional dress—deer hoof/skin armband, bead and shell gorget, and eagle feathers—documenting Cree adornment and dress.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Documentary photograph of six Cree men in regalia (feather headdresses, fringed garments, one on horseback) following a Sun Dance ceremony at Battleford, 1895 — clear ethnographic depiction of Cree dress and custom.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Documentary photograph of a group of Cree men gathered at a sun dance lodge in Battleford, Saskatchewan, wearing headdresses, feathers, and mixed traditional/western clothing — a clear ethnographic scene of Cree ceremonial life.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Documentary photograph of Native chiefs and their sons in traditional dress with tepees in the background, taken at Battleford (Treaty 6 / Plains Cree territory) in 1895 — a genuine ethnographic record of dress and daily life consistent with the Cree claim.

photo.name: photographic print; glass negative
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); glass negative
photo.reason: The image shows a Plains man on horseback wearing a feather warbonnet, decorated leggings and moccasins, a documentary-style photo of dress plausible for a Cree/Plains community as recorded by the museum.

household.name: purse
household.title: purse
household.reason: A moosehide purse with floral beadwork and a shoulder strap, a classic Cree craft item made of traditional materials with beaded decoration.

household.name: Bag
household.title: Panel Bag
household.reason: The bag is a quilled and beaded hide panel bag attributed to Cree-Métis makers (ca. 1840), a classic Subarctic/Métis floral and geometric beadwork style, matching the claimed Cree ethnicity.

household.name: rifle-case
household.title: rifle-case
household.reason: A grey felted wool rifle case with floral silk-thread embroidery and a moose-skin closure, a classic Cree/Métis-style beaded-or-embroidered gun case, museum credits it as made by Cree. This matches known Cree floral embroidery craft traditions.

household.name: baby-carrier
household.title: baby-carrier
household.reason: A moose-hide and cotton baby-carrier bag, a household item made and used by Cree people; moose-hide trim and cotton with rickrack decoration is typical of Cree craft work.

household.name: Bag
household.title: Firebag
household.reason: This is a classic Northern Plains/Subarctic beaded "firebag" (fire-steel/tobacco pouch) with quillwork-style floral beadwork and wool/silk trade cloth, a type made and used by Cree and neighboring Ojibwa groups; the museum's own attribution names Cree as a possibility, so it belongs.

household.name: rifle-case
household.title: rifle-case
household.reason: A denim rifle-case sewn with moose-skin closure, ric-rac trim, and floral beadwork/embroidery bands typical of Cree craftwork, documented as made by Cree. Fits the claimed ethnicity and category as a used/made household item.

textile.name: bag
textile.title: bag
textile.reason: A dark blue velvet drawstring bag with floral glass beadwork, a classic Cree/Métis-style beaded bag made and used by the Cree; the museum explicitly attributes it to Cree makers.

painting-mss.name: picture
painting-mss.title: picture
painting-mss.reason: Birchbark bitework showing four stylized birds arranged in a symmetrical pattern — a traditional Cree/Algonquian craft technique (makak-style biting art), well attested among Cree women, and the museum attributes it to Cree makers.
